parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the full Java coursework scope: 17 requirement slugs spanning experiments and homework, exact test-called signatures, data files, compilation expectations, and the instruction not to stop early.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It prepared reference material from original class files, launched a broad workflow with module-level implementers plus verification, then used later parent-led continuation and audit work to close remaining gaps.
parallel.implementation: The implementation path restored stubbed Java methods from decompiled references and from direct edits across the homework and experiment directories; later checks reported all 17 modules compiling and zero TODO stubs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent kept the workspace as the final integration point, committed requirement patches, compiled all modules together with a local script, and delivered the repaired source tree for official evaluation.
parallel.verification: Verification included per-module child compile/run checks, a whole-project compile_all run, audit workflow results, and finally a completed official LoopsBench evaluation with all listed tests passed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The first broad workflow suffered API 429 and non-retrieval/stopped protocol problems, but the later continuation recovered before official evaluation; no required module remained failing in the final status.

serial.requirements: The serial run had the same prompt and recognized the broad 17-module requirement list, including the git patch workflow and the warning that partial fixes would fail.
serial.plan_and_ownership: It proceeded as a single local agent, committing one requirement at a time and using decompiled class references, with no workflow children or delegation observed in status.
serial.implementation: The serial path completed useful early work such as DS02 linked list, DS02 string, and DS01, then began decompiling the remaining experiments and homework modules late in the run.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Serial commits and patch files were made for completed early requirements, but the final delivered tree still lacked functioning implementations for many later modules.
serial.verification: Serial ran focused compile and scripted checks for completed pieces, but it did not reach an all-module compile/audit closure comparable to the parallel run before official evaluation.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official status shows failures across loser tree, priority queue, farmer, island lake, project, tree building, graph traversal, BST/search, hash, and red-black tree tests, making the serial attempt incomplete.

outcome_analysis.explanation: This is a parallel_only_pass. The parallel run won because it used workflow delegation and later parent recovery to implement, integrate, and verify the full 17-module Java coursework, ending with zero TODO stubs, all module compile checks ok, audit checks, and a completed official pass. The serial run stayed single-agent and made correct progress on early requirements, but it was still starting the remaining experiment/reference decompilation path late in round 3 and the official evaluation failed broad uncompleted module groups.
parallel_contributors: Broad module-level workflow decomposition gave the parallel attempt enough throughput to cover the full 17-requirement surface.
Parent-led recovery after the first workflow failure checked current workspace state, removed remaining stubs, compiled all modules, and consumed later audit results.
Whole-project compile and official final tests established end-to-end acceptance before closure.
serial_contributors: The serial control avoided delegation but advanced one requirement at a time, completing only early DS01/DS02 work before moving to remaining experiment decompilation.

The final serial workspace lacked working implementations for many later modules, as shown by official failures across graph, tree, search, hash, red-black-tree, priority queue, loser tree, farmer, island lake, and project tests.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial incompleteness is an ordinary throughput and implementation-coverage shortfall, not a parallel coordination label.
Parallel restored reference-faithful Java behavior across modules that serial had not yet reached.
